Add HTTP retry handling to Task SDK.
pr_comments: Merging as (still) no response from Kaxil/Ash... let me know "post mortem" if some polishing is needed.

issue_context.title: Add HTTP retry handling into task sdk's api.client
comments: Might be related to proposal in #44536 - I'd propose to have (at least parameters) in common

review_comments:
Two things here:

1. Currently, the API_RETRIES, API_RETRY_WAIT_MIN, and API_RETRY_WAIT_MAX are directly cast to integers. This can raise a ValueError if the environment variables are not set correctly. Can we add validation or some fallback defaults (In case of error, if we don't want to fail)?
2. Let's also have a check, `API_RETRY_WAIT_MIN < API_RETRY_WAIT_MAX` and raise alarm if not ?

Good points. But as in the comments above it is referring to a "proper config mechanism" which is missing. Would leave it up there.
The values at the end are passed to tenacity, even there in the logic it seems to be no validation. If you "mess-up" the values then it will use the max as minimum it seems. Not too bad.

For me it is okay like this, except if @kaxil or @ashb would also enforce me to make it bullet-proof here. My aim was that it is working by default but that the defaults can be over-ridden. No "official" config but something that can be tweaked if you are looking into code.
2. is already handled in the tenacity library. We do not have to explicitly handle that
Ohh this makes sense then @jscheffl , thanks!
Good point. Thanks for the proposal. Consolidated now... but w/o fixture as this does not provide a benefit over a "normal" utility like it was there before.
Should we replace the client initialisation in all the other test classes to use `make_client_w_responses` instead?

I briefly thought about it but if you take a look how the other tests are mocking the backend ... there are conditions and asserts in request handling implemented. So the other mock has a different test level. So I decided to move both close together but they have a different implementation demand.

Yeah, and we need those validations too.

One thing however that we can do is, add test under each endpoint class like "task instance, "variables" etc using the client with retries just to test the fact that those subpaths work.
Added a test per test class such that a retry is contained in other tests now as well.
